findings.title: Success criteria coverage, ordering and test pairing
findings.description:
- **Coverage:** all ten functional criteria and the four technical criteria map to tasks (auto-init to Tasks 9–21, rename and alias to 1–8, `cf init --strategy` and help to 25–27, managed notice and docs to 28–31, walkthrough to 32).
- **Scope:** no task falls outside the design.
- **Ordering:** follows the design's suggested order, and each implementation task is followed by its test task.
- **Load test:** the slice restates no NFR (review F006), so none is required.
- **Size:** 32 tasks is heavy but fits three issues across three packages.

findings.title: Task 13 relies on a `/timed out/i` pattern that does not exist
findings.description: Task 13 says the timeout message will get remediation text because "the `/timed out/i` pattern already matches". The actual entries in `NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERNS` are `/connection timed out/i` and `/etimedout/i`. A message such as "git … timed out after 60 seconds" matches neither, so `withNetworkErrorHint` returns it unchanged. Task 14's assertion on `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION` would then fail with no step telling the implementer why. Add an explicit Task 13 step: either add a pattern for the new timeout message or word the message to match an existing one.

findings.title: D10 timeout wiring is contradictory in Task 15 and never tested
findings.description:
Task 15 gives the signature `init(operationPath: string)` with the timeout hard-wired. Its next bullet says the timeout is "an `init()` option" so that `sync()` stays unbounded. Task 17 then calls `SubmoduleStrategy.init(operationPath)` with no option.

If the option defaults to off, the auto-init fetch is unbounded and D10 (the resolution of review concern F004) is unmet. No test would catch this:
- Task 14 tests `gitExec` in isolation.
- Tasks 16 and 18 never assert that a timeout reaches `gitExec`.

Fix by pinning the signature and which caller passes the timeout. Add one assertion in Task 16 or 18 that the auto-init path passes `GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, and one that `sync()` does not.

findings.title: Task 11 makes `detect()` throw, breaking existing mocked tests with no update step
findings.description:
Task 11 has `detect()` throw when `checkSyncStatus()` returns `'error'`. The existing submodule cases mock `gitExec` to reject everything except `describe`, so `git submodule status` rejects and those tests will throw. Task 4 only covers rename expectations, and Tasks 11–12 have no step for updating these mocks.

Other suites that mock `gitExec` around `detect()` may be affected too; I did not check them. Add a Task 11 step to update the mocks and run the full core, CLI and MCP suites before the Task 12 commit.

The same step should state which `detect()` callers the new throw is intended for. `cf version --json` (packages/cli/src/index.ts:136-143) swallows it and would report `guideVersion: null`.

findings.title: Task 22 under-specifies the MCP wiring and would make `template_preview` auto-init
findings.description:
- **Shared helper:** line 57 sits inside `generateContext()`, which `template_preview` also uses. That tool is annotated `readOnlyHint: true` and described as having no side effects, and it is not in the design's list. Calling `ensureCheckout()` there makes it fetch and write a checkout. The task must say where the call goes and what `template_preview` does.
- **Notices shape:** `generateContext()` and `resolvePromptFileForTools()` both return `Promise<string>`, and results are built by `textResult`/`jsonResult`. The task never says how a notice leaves the helper or where `notices` sits on a text result. Task 7 introduces `notices` first, yet the "one shared shape" criterion appears only in Task 22. Define the shape once, before Task 7.
- **Missing grep:** D3 requires grepping `packages/mcp-server/src` as well; only Task 20 (CLI) has the grep step.
- **Test coverage:** Task 23 tests `context_build` only. `prompt_list` and `prompt_get` are named in the design's data flow but have no auto-init test.

findings.title: Task 5's "no fallback branch is needed" ignores the optional `configManager`
findings.description: `configManager` is an optional constructor argument (line 15), and the `'submodule'` literal at line 196 is also the path taken when none is injected. Task 5 says to return `normalizeGuideMethod(configValue)` from `ConfigManager.get()` and delete the literal, with no word on the no-manager case. A literal reading forces the implementer to make the manager required or reintroduce a default. State the intended source, which D6 names as `ConfigKeys['guide.git_strategy'].default`. Add a Task 6 case for a `GuideManager` built without a `ConfigManager`.

findings.title: Task 7 permits `manual` literals that Task 32 and the design forbid
findings.description: Task 7 adds `'manual'` to the MCP zod enum and its success criterion allows "the MCP enum entry and deprecation-message text". The design's technical criterion, repeated in Task 32, allows the literal only in the alias table and the `ConfigKeys` enum. As written the Task 32 check fails. Either build the zod enum and deprecation text from the canonical values plus `GUIDE_METHOD_DEPRECATED_ALIASES` (Task 1 already exports it), or amend the Task 32 check to name the allowed exceptions.

findings.title: Commit instructions are embedded in checkbox items
findings.description: All 14 commit points are written as "Commit: `…`" inside a `- [ ] Success criteria:` checkbox, not as plain `**Commit**:` lines. The box cannot be truthfully checked before the commit that is supposed to include the check-off. Placement is sound: each sits after a tested point, and none falls in the deliberately broken Task 1–3 window. Move each to its own plain `**Commit**:` line after the task.

findings.title: Smaller items
findings.description:
- **Task 10:** its success criterion is "typecheck passes once Task 11 populates the field", so it cannot be verified alone. Merge it into Task 11.
- **Task 8:** it tests the deprecation warning only for the `--strategy manual` flag. The criterion "shared config `manual` installs with the same warning" has no CLI assertion that the warning is printed; one case would cover it.
- **Task 17:** it appends `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION` to errors that `gitExec` has already extended via `withNetworkErrorHint` (gitExec.ts:46-49). Network failures will print the remediation twice.
- **Task 20:** the enumerated call sites omit `packages/cli/src/utils/phaseShorthand.ts:22`, which the prescribed grep will hit. Say whether the `prompt.ts` calls cover it.
- **Task 26:** it passes `normalizeGuideMethod(opts.strategy)` unconditionally, which throws when the flag is omitted. Say "only when provided".
- **Task 32:** "PM reviews before merge to `main`" is not something the implementer can verify. Drop it from the success criteria.
